name: VLA-JEPA
summary: VLA-JEPA attacks a specific failure of world-model pretraining for policies: reconstruct-the-future objectives spend capacity on pixel variation — camera shake, lighting, background motion — that has nothing to do with what the action changed. It supervises the policy with a joint-embedding predictive architecture instead, using leakage-free state prediction in which a target encoder sees future frames while the student sees only the current observation, forcing the representation to encode action-relevant state change. The result collapses the multi-stage latent-action pipelines of earlier work into two stages: JEPA pretraining, then action-head fine-tuning. It reports consistent gains on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, SimplerEnv and real manipulation, with the largest margins under out-of-distribution camera and background shifts. Accepted at ECCV 2026.
innovation: Leakage-free target/student split that keeps latent prediction from degenerating into copying the observation.
Reduces latent-action pretraining to two stages, removing the separate quantizer and inverse-dynamics phases earlier methods needed.
matters: The academic-scale counterweight to DreamZero: it shows the world-action gain comes from predicting dynamics, not specifically from generating video, which is enormously cheaper.
limits: Gains are measured mostly on simulation suites; the real-robot evaluation is small.
Latent prediction gives up the interpretability of a generated video plan — you cannot look at what the model expects to happen.
lineage: V-JEPA 2's joint-embedding prediction moved inside a VLA's pretraining loop.
